title: Postoperative care of patient with low anterior resections syndrome (LARS) after rectal cancer surgery - a multicenter, open, prospective, randomized comparative trial with two follow-up care regimes
summary:
The study is about intestinal dysfunction after stoma repositioning after surgery for a rectal tumor.
Bowel dysfunction may occur in up to 80% of patients who have undergone a sphincter-preserving rectal resection for rectal cancer or stoma repositioning. The functional disorders can develop immediately after the operation and are accompanied by symptoms such as fecal incontinence, difficulty emptying stools, the urge to defecate that cannot be postponed or increased stool frequency. This represents a significant reduction in the quality of life for patients. These symptoms are summarized under the name LARS (Low Anterior Resection Syndrome). Despite the frequency, there are hardly any treatment concepts in everyday care.
Different methods for treating LARS include: dietary advice, drug therapy (e.g. bulking agents, psyllium), physiotherapy (e.g. muscular pelvic floor training), emptying aids (e.g. clysters, transanal irrigation (a mechanical system for bowel emptying)), neuromodulation (e.g. sacral nerve stimulation - a a so-called pelvic floor pacemaker that sends gentle electronic impulses to bring the intestines back into balance). In severe cases, a permanent stoma may make sense.
The aim of the study is to examine whether the quality of life differs in relation to two different aftercare concepts over a period of one year. Patients in group A receive intensive functional follow-up care by being contacted by the treating physician every 3 months. Group B patients receive standardized follow-up care (information about LARS symptoms, treatment recommendations) and are asked to contact their doctor if they have any problems.
The following data will be collected at defined dates: Group A and Group B at T1 (6 weeks after hospital discharge) and T5 (13 months after hospital discharge) - LARS symptoms, adherence to prescribed therapy, questions about quality of life, psychosocial questions about anxiety and stress symptoms , depression. Group A additionally on T 2, 3 and 4 (each after 3 months) - LARS symptoms and adherence to the prescribed therapy.
All patients who come to the clinic for repositioning of a temporary stoma after deep anterior rectal resection for the treatment of rectal cancer are potential study patients and can be screened for participation. Only patients who actually develop LARS will be included.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Age at least 18 years and full legal capacity
• Signed informed consent (ICF)
• Rectal resection for rectal cancer
• Surgery for stoma repositioning after initial total mesorectal excision (TME) with protective stoma creation
• LARS (minor/major), detected 4 weeks after hospital discharge (after stoma repositioning)
• Completion of any adjuvant therapy that may have been indicated
• Be able and willing to meet all study appointments as required by the protocol
• Be able and willing to complete study-related documents
Exclusion criteria:
Participation in other stoma studies
• UICC stage IV
• Multivisceral resections
• Insufficient German language skills and/or hearing loss
• Pregnancy/Breastfeeding
